import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Boxdot Conjecture

The Boxdot Conjecture was originally formulated by French and Humberstone and
has been studied in several works. In particular, see:

*References:*
- [arxiv/1308.0994](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0994)
  **Cluster Expansion and the Boxdot Conjecture** by *Emil Jeřábek*
- [The Boxdot Conjecture and the Generalized McKinsey Axiom](https://ojs.victoria.ac.nz/ajl/article/view/4891)
  by *Christopher Steinsvold*, Australasian Journal of Logic

-/

namespace Arxiv.«1308.0994»

/--
`Formula` is the inductive type of propositional modal formulas:

* `Atom n` is a propositional variable indexed by `n`.
* `Falsum` is the constant ⊥.
* `Imp α β` is implication `(α → β)`.
* `Nec α` is the necessity operator `□α`.
-/
inductive Formula : Type
  /-- `Atom n` is a propositional variable indexed by `n`. -/
  | Atom : Nat → Formula
  /--  `Falsum` is the constant ⊥. -/
  | Falsum : Formula
  /-- `Imp α β` is implication `(α → β)`. -/
  | Imp : Formula → Formula → Formula
  /-- `Nec α` is the necessity operator `□α`. -/
  | Nec : Formula → Formula

open Formula

@[inherit_doc Falsum]
scoped notation "⊥" => Falsum

@[inherit_doc Imp]
infixr:80 " ~> " => Formula.Imp

/-- `~ α` is the negation of `α`. `~ α` is also equivalent to `α ~> ⊥`. -/
scoped notation:max " ~ " φ => φ ~> ⊥

@[inherit_doc Nec]
scoped prefix:95 "□" => Nec

/-- `Conj α β` is the conjunction `α ∧ β`. We define `α & β` as `~(α ~> ~β)` for simplicity. -/
@[reducible]
def Conj (α β : Formula) : Formula := ~(α ~> ~β)

@[inherit_doc Conj]
scoped infixr:85 " & " => Conj

/--
`t φ` is the Boxdot translation of a formula `φ`. Roughly, t is the mapping `φ ↦ t φ`
from the language of monomodal logic into itself that preserves variables and the logical constant `⊥`,
commutes with the standard truth-functional operators, and is such that `t □a` = `□t a & t a`.
This implementation follows the definition in Steinsvold (AJL).
-/
def t (φ : Formula) : Formula :=
  match φ with
  | α ~> β => t α ~> t β
  | □α => □t α & t α
  | _ => φ

@[inherit_doc t]
scoped prefix:95 "■" => t


/--
`KProof Γ φ` is the usual Hilbert‐style proof relation for the minimal normal modal logic K,
with assumptions drawn from `Γ`.
-/
inductive KProof : Set Formula → Formula → Prop
/-- Assumption rule: if `α ∈ Γ` then `α` is provable from `Γ`. -/
| ax {Γ} {α} (h : α ∈ Γ) : KProof Γ α
/-- Ax1: every instance of the schema `α → (β → α)` is a theorem. -/
| ax1 {Γ} {α β} : KProof Γ (α ~> β ~> α)
/-- Ax2: every instance of the schema `(α ~> β ~> γ) ~> (α ~> β) ~> (α ~> γ)` is a theorem. -/
| ax2 {Γ} {α β γ} : KProof Γ ((α ~> β ~> γ) ~> (α ~> β) ~> (α ~> γ))
/-- Ax3 (contraposition): every instance of the schema `(~α ~> ~β) ~> (β ~> α)` is a theorem. -/
| ax3 {Γ} {α β} : KProof Γ (((~α) ~> (~β)) ~> (β ~> α))
/-- Modus Ponens: if `Γ ⊢ α ~> β` and `Γ ⊢ α`, then `Γ ⊢ β`. -/
| mp {Γ} {α β} (_ : KProof Γ (α ~> β)) (_ : KProof Γ α) : KProof Γ β
/-- Necessitation: if `⊢ α` then `⊢ □α`. -/
| nec {Γ} {α} (_ : KProof ∅ α) : KProof Γ (□ α)
/-- Distribution: every instance of the schema `□(α ~> β) ~> (□α ~> □β)` is a theorem. -/
| distr {Γ} {α β} : KProof Γ (□ (α ~> β) ~> □ α ~> □ β)


/--
`KTProof Γ φ` denotes that `φ` is provable from the premises `Γ` in the normal modal logic KT
(also called T). KT extends system K by adding the instances of the T-axiom schema `□φ ~> φ` to K’s
usual axioms and rules of inference.
-/
inductive KTProof : Set Formula → Formula → Prop
/-- Embedding of K proofs into KT. -/
| lift_K {Γ} {α} (h : KProof Γ α) : KTProof Γ α
/-- T-axiom schema: every instance of `□α ~> α` is a theorem. -/
| axT {Γ} {α} : KTProof Γ (□ α ~> α)
/-- Modus Ponens: if `Γ ⊢ α ~> β` and `Γ ⊢ α`, then `Γ ⊢ β`. -/
| mp {Γ} {α β} (_ : KTProof Γ (α ~> β)) (_ : KTProof Γ α) : KTProof Γ β
/-- Necessitation: if `⊢ α` then `⊢ □α`. -/
| nec {Γ} {α} (_ : KTProof ∅ α) : KTProof Γ (□ α)


open KProof KTProof


/--
If `KProof Γ φ`, then `KTProof Γ φ`. In other words, KT extends K.
-/
@[category API, AMS 3]
lemma KTExtendsK {Γ φ} (h : KProof Γ φ) : KTProof Γ φ :=
  lift_K h

/--
A “normal modal logic” L is any `Set Formula` such that:
  1. If `K ⊢ φ`, then `φ ∈ L`          (L extends K)
  2. If `φ ∈ L` and `(φ ~> ψ) ∈ L`, then `ψ ∈ L`  (Closed under MP)
  3. If `φ ∈ L`, then `□φ ∈ L`          (Closed under Necessitation)
-/
structure NormalModalLogic : Type where
  /-- `thms` is the set of formulas proveable in the logic. -/
  thms : Set Formula
  /-- `extK` means that if `K ⊢ φ`, then `φ ∈ thms`. That is, the logic extends system K. -/
  extK : ∀ {φ}, KProof ∅ φ → φ ∈ thms
  /-- `mp` means that if `φ ∈ thms` and `(φ ~> ψ) ∈ thms`, then `ψ ∈ thms`. That is, thms is closed
  under modus ponens. -/
  mp : ∀ {φ ψ}, φ ∈ thms → (φ ~> ψ) ∈ thms → ψ ∈ thms
  /-- `nec` means that if `φ ∈ thms`, then `□φ ∈ thms`. Equivalently, `thms` is closed under
  necessitation -/
  nec : ∀ {φ}, φ ∈ thms → □ φ ∈ thms


def proves (L : NormalModalLogic) (φ : Formula) := φ ∈ L.thms

scoped infixr:85 " ⊢ " => proves

/--
`KT` is the specific normal modal logic whose theorems are exactly those provable
in `KTProof` from the empty context.

This corresponds to `K ⊕ (□φ → φ)` as in both AJL (Steinsvold) and Jeřábek.
-/
def KT : NormalModalLogic := by
  constructor
  case thms =>
    exact {φ | KTProof ∅ φ}
  case extK =>
    intro _ h
    exact KTExtendsK h
  case mp =>
    intro φ ψ h₁ h₂
    simp [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at *
    exact KTProof.mp h₂ h₁
  case nec =>
    intro φ h
    simp [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at *
    exact KTProof.nec h


/--
Boxdot Conjecture: every normal modal logic that faithfully interprets KT
by the boxdot translation is included in KT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/FormalizedFormalLogic/Foundation"]
-- The formal proof was done by Mashu Noguchi et al.
-- see linked repo for the full list of contributors
theorem BoxdotConjecture (L : NormalModalLogic) (H : ∀ φ, L ⊢ ■ φ ↔ KT ⊢ φ) : L.thms ⊆ KT.thms := by
  sorry

end Arxiv.«1308.0994»

findings.description: The structure requires only `extK`, `mp`, and `nec`; it omits closure under uniform substitution. Consequently, `BoxdotConjecture` quantifies over necessitation-closed K-theories, a strictly larger domain than the source's normal modal logics. This condition is not implied even by the faithfulness hypothesis H. In `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, I constructed L = KT ∩ Th(M), where M has one world, no accessibility edges, p₀ true, and all other atoms false. Lean verifies that L satisfies all existing structure fields and H, but contains `□p₀ → p₀` while omitting its substitution instance `□p₁ → p₁`. Thus this is not an equivalent characterization of the source's domain. This example distinguishes the definitions; it is not a counterexample to the inclusion conclusion, since this particular L is contained in KT.
findings.source_evidence: French and Humberstone, the original paper cited by both references, explicitly define the term on p. 57, footnote 2: a normal modal logic contains all K-theorems and is closed under 'Necessitation, Modus Ponens, and Uniform Substitution' (https://ojs.victoria.ac.nz/ajl/article/download/1808/1659). Steinsvold, p. 630, states the conjecture 'for all normal modal logics L' (https://ojs.victoria.ac.nz/ajl/article/download/4891/4345); Jeřábek §1 likewise quantifies over normal modal logics (https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0994).
findings.suggested_fix: Define structural substitution `Formula.subst (σ : ℕ → Formula)`, replacing `Atom n` by `σ n` and commuting with Falsum, implication, and necessity. Add a field `subst_closed : ∀ (σ : ℕ → Formula) {φ}, φ ∈ thms → Formula.subst σ φ ∈ thms` to `NormalModalLogic`. Supply this field for KT by induction on its proofs; substitution admissibility for both proof systems was checked in the scratch file.

status_issues.source_status: The located external formalization proves the source result for `Logic.IsNormal`, which explicitly includes uniform substitution. It therefore does not directly establish the broader assertion quantified over the file's current `NormalModalLogic`. This concerns the formal-proof record's scope, not the `research solved` tag: Jeřábek did prove the original conjecture in 2013.
status_issues.evidence: The historical proof in https://github.com/FormalizedFormalLogic/Foundation/blob/87d4dd68835a6c1eb8448b9c392d9ca51fe08d63/Foundation/Modal/Boxdot/Jerabek.lean uses `L.IsNormal` in `StrongBoxdotProperty` and `BoxdotProperty`; https://github.com/FormalizedFormalLogic/Foundation/blob/87d4dd68835a6c1eb8448b9c392d9ca51fe08d63/Foundation/Modal/Logic/Basic.lean makes `IsNormal` inherit `Substitution`. The same assumptions remain in the current ModalLogicArchive copy.
status_issues.suggested_change: Keep `research solved`. After adding the missing substitution closure, retain the formal-proof annotation with a stable, precise link to the external proof. If the broader theory-level formulation is intentional, verify a formal proof covering that broader domain before treating this annotation as certification of it.

reformulations.difference: Jeřábek writes the translated necessity as `t φ ∧ □t φ`, whereas the file uses `□t φ & t φ`, following Steinsvold exactly. Conjunction is encoded using implication and falsum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The encoded conjunction has the classical conjunction truth table. Commutativity at the necessity clause, followed by structural induction, proves equivalence of the two translations on every Kripke model. The scratch file proves this semantic biconditional as `Review.source_translation_equiv`. Thus the conjunction order does not change the conjecture.

reformulations.difference: The proof systems use local consequence for nonempty premise sets: necessitation requires an empty-context proof. Jeřábek's Definition 2.6 instead introduces global consequence, allowing necessitation of consequences of premises.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The conjecture uses only empty-context K and KT proofs. At the empty context, local and global derivability coincide by induction on derivations: unrestricted necessitation there still acts on an empty-context proof. The auxiliary inclusion `KTExtendsK` is valid under either convention. Hence the distinction in unused nonempty-context behavior does not alter the problem stated.

review.notes: All declarations were reviewed. The formula grammar, classical axioms, K/KT theorem sets, translation, inclusion direction, and quantifier scope otherwise agree with the sources. The omission identified above enlarges the domain; I am not claiming that the enlarged theorem is false—Jeřábek's argument appears to extend to it. The scratch file compiles and independently proves the faithful non-substitution-closed example, K/KT substitution admissibility, `KProof ∅ (t φ) ↔ KTProof ∅ φ`, and the semantic translation equivalence. demonstrated.claim: An object of NormalModalLogic can contain Atom 0 while excluding Falsum, which uniform substitution of falsum for that atom forbids in a standard normal modal logic.

import FormalConjectures.Arxiv.«1308.0994».BoxdotConjecture

/-! A fixed valuation gives an admitted theory that is not a normal modal logic.
This tests the structure alone, not the faithfulness hypothesis of the conjecture. -/
namespace BoxdotDefinitionTest

-- Truth at one reflexive world, with every propositional variable true.
private def truth : Arxiv.«1308.0994».Formula → Prop
  | Arxiv.«1308.0994».Formula.Atom _ => True
  | Arxiv.«1308.0994».Formula.Falsum => False
  | Arxiv.«1308.0994».Formula.Imp a b => truth a → truth b
  | Arxiv.«1308.0994».Formula.Nec a => truth a

private lemma k_sound {Γ : Set Arxiv.«1308.0994».Formula} {φ}
    (h : Arxiv.«1308.0994».KProof Γ φ) :
    (∀ ψ ∈ Γ, truth ψ) → truth φ := by
  induction h <;> simp_all [truth]
  tauto

private def fixedValuation : Arxiv.«1308.0994».NormalModalLogic where
  thms := {φ | truth φ}
  extK h := k_sound h (by simp)
  mp hφ hφψ := hφψ hφ
  nec hφ := hφ

-- Arxiv.«1308.0994».NormalModalLogic admits an atom without falsum,
-- impossible for a normal modal logic: uniformly substitute falsum for that atom.
theorem admits_non_substitution_closed_theory :
    ∃ L : Arxiv.«1308.0994».NormalModalLogic,
      Arxiv.«1308.0994».Formula.Atom 0 ∈ L.thms ∧
      Arxiv.«1308.0994».Formula.Falsum ∉ L.thms := by
  exact ⟨fixedValuation, True.intro, id⟩

#print axioms admits_non_substitution_closed_theory
end BoxdotDefinitionTest

submission.summary: Added structural uniform substitution and required closure under it in NormalModalLogic, matching the source's definition. Proved substitution admissibility for KProof and KTProof and supplied the new closure field for KT. The edited file compiles with only the existing conjecture's sorry warning; regression checks confirm the previous non-substitution-closed example is excluded.

/-- Ax2: every instance of the schema `(α ~> β ~> γ) ~> (α ~> β) ~> (α ~> γ)` is a theorem. -/

open KProof KTProof


/--
If `KProof Γ φ`, then `KTProof Γ φ`. In other words, KT extends K.
-/
@[category API, AMS 3]
lemma KTExtendsK {Γ φ} (h : KProof Γ φ) : KTProof Γ φ :=
  lift_K h

/-- Uniform substitution preserves K-proofs, with the same substitution applied to the premises. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
lemma KProof.subst {Γ : Set Formula} {φ : Formula} (h : KProof Γ φ) (σ : ℕ → Formula) :
    KProof (Formula.subst σ '' Γ) (Formula.subst σ φ) := by
  induction h with
  | ax h => exact KProof.ax ⟨_, h, rfl⟩
  | ax1 => exact KProof.ax1
  | ax2 => exact KProof.ax2
  | ax3 => exact KProof.ax3
  | mp _ _ ih₁ ih₂ => exact KProof.mp ih₁ ih₂
  | nec _ ih =>
      apply KProof.nec
      simpa only [Set.image_empty] using ih
  | distr => exact KProof.distr

/-- Uniform substitution preserves KT-proofs, with the same substitution applied to the premises. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
lemma KTProof.subst {Γ : Set Formula} {φ : Formula} (h : KTProof Γ φ) (σ : ℕ → Formula) :
    KTProof (Formula.subst σ '' Γ) (Formula.subst σ φ) := by
  induction h with
  | lift_K h => exact KTProof.lift_K (KProof.subst h σ)
  | axT => exact KTProof.axT
  | mp _ _ ih₁ ih₂ => exact KTProof.mp ih₁ ih₂
  | nec _ ih =>

      simpa only [Set.image_empty] using ih

  2. If `φ ∈ L` and `(φ ~> ψ) ∈ L`, then `ψ ∈ L`  (Closed under MP)
  3. If `φ ∈ L`, then `□φ ∈ L`          (Closed under Necessitation)
  4. If `φ ∈ L`, then `Formula.subst σ φ ∈ L` for every `σ` (Closed under Uniform Substitution)
-/
structure NormalModalLogic : Type where
  /-- `thms` is the set of formulas proveable in the logic. -/
  thms : Set Formula
  /-- `extK` means that if `K ⊢ φ`, then `φ ∈ thms`. That is, the logic extends system K. -/
  extK : ∀ {φ}, KProof ∅ φ → φ ∈ thms
  /-- `mp` means that if `φ ∈ thms` and `(φ ~> ψ) ∈ thms`, then `ψ ∈ thms`. That is, thms is closed
  under modus ponens. -/
  mp : ∀ {φ ψ}, φ ∈ thms → (φ ~> ψ) ∈ thms → ψ ∈ thms

  nec : ∀ {φ}, φ ∈ thms → □ φ ∈ thms
  /-- Every uniform substitution of a theorem is a theorem. -/
  subst_closed : ∀ (σ : ℕ → Formula) {φ}, φ ∈ thms → Formula.subst σ φ ∈ thms


def proves (L : NormalModalLogic) (φ : Formula) := φ ∈ L.thms

scoped infixr:85 " ⊢ " => proves

/--
`KT` is the specific normal modal logic whose theorems are exactly those provable
in `KTProof` from the empty context.

This corresponds to `K ⊕ (□φ → φ)` as in both AJL (Steinsvold) and Jeřábek.
-/
def KT : NormalModalLogic := by
  constructor
  case thms =>
    exact {φ | KTProof ∅ φ}
  case extK =>
    intro _ h
    exact KTExtendsK h
  case mp =>
    intro φ ψ h₁ h₂
    simp [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at *
    exact KTProof.mp h₂ h₁
  case nec =>
    intro φ h
    simp [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at *
    exact KTProof.nec h
  case subst_closed =>
    intro σ φ h
    simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq] at *
    simpa only [Set.image_empty] using KTProof.subst h σ


/--
Boxdot Conjecture: every normal modal logic that faithfully interprets KT
by the boxdot translation is included in KT.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/FormalizedFormalLogic/Foundation"]
-- The formal proof was done by Mashu Noguchi et al.
-- see linked repo for the full list of contributors
theorem BoxdotConjecture (L : NormalModalLogic) (H : ∀ φ, L ⊢ ■ φ ↔ KT ⊢ φ) : L.thms ⊆ KT.thms := by
  sorry

end Arxiv.«1308.0994»
